main_text.l: ditatio, mádata divinitus omnibus vitæ humanæ ordinibus, inprimis verò his qui alios cum fructu docere volunt. Meditationem definit lectionem, quia sensum & succum Scripturæ non tam oculari inspectione, quam præsentis animi attetione & solerti indagine venamur & assequimur:(Psal.1.v.2.) Hac Meditationem in medio quasi locat inter duo extrema, negligentiam & sophisticen, negligentiæ tanquam defectui opponens diligentiam, sophisticæ autem (quâ alius Scripturæ præter genuinū, sensus affingitur) velut excessui, iudicium sanū. Ad huiusmodi diligentem cum sano iudicio & euidenti utilitate coniū-ctam Verbi divini lectionem seu meditationem, hac meâ apellâ viâ sternere conatus, ea quæ à doctissi-mis quibusvis Theologis recentio•

page.notes: The last word "ribus," sits alone at the right below the final line, so it is recorded as a catchword; it may instead be the continuation of "recentio•ribus,". The bullet after "recentio" is a printer's mark, not text. A dot at the top right is a stray mark and was left out. "mádata" carries an accent as printed and is uncertain. "sophisticen" is printed as such. The facing page's edge at the right is not transcribed.
